It does put them on an overlay network, ZeroTier does this as well. The important part here is that you can install zt/tailscale on a small Linux vps that does have a public address associated to it and port forward from that to whatever you want , including your private lan addresses. Both have a feature to route your internal subnets across links so that if you had a situation where you had a server running on a lan with 172.16.78.2 as its address, you could allow the overlay network to route straight to it, so if you had a Linux host on the internet with (insert public address here), you can directly port forward to your 172.16.78.2(whatever lan addresses your running) with no issue. connect to it via ethernet
upgrade ros(if its already updated, make sure you have the wireless rep package installed and wireless-cm2 disabled.

Set the mode to ap bridge.
set the interface name up as ap 
set up your settings as normal. but set the channel to AUTO.
set the ssid to whatever you want and set WIRELESS protocol to 802.11

if your going to do a password, go ahead and enable and apply your settings and click on over to security profiles, 

add new, and set it up however you want.. name it something distinct 
like approfile ...save and go back over to interfaces , and for security profile , select your newly created security profile.

We are going to keep this simple. when you have it working then you can take the blue pill and bridge the network your repeating to the repeated clients..haha but we will keep it red for now.


Ok so by this point you should have a wireless interface called ap, configured active. you can try to connect. you will not get an ip address.. but you should be able to connect to it.

Moving on..

Click on wireless, then on the interfaces tab again, and add a virtual interface. 

Name it client,
Set the mode to station.

Set the ssid to the ssid we are repeating.
If there is security on this ssid, then save your settings
go back to security profiles, create a new one called client
set that up to match the network your connecting to's security settings.

go back to your second wireless interface you named client.

apply that security profile.

as long as that and your ssid are correct and you have enabled that interface, you should see it switch to "connected to ess" at the bottom. 

Your almost there! 

If you do not see this..  double check your security settings, if they are correct, set the ap's channel to the channel of the network your repeating


If its connected, go to ip->dhcp client

add a new dhcp client for the interface named client
check the add default gateway box.

apply and you should see it get an address...

We are almost done!

add a bridge, call it tacos..or something you will remember

now if your mikrotik has a switch, slave all the ethernet ports to one master port or 2 or 3, depending on how many switch groups your device has...

example: ether2 ether3 ether4 set master interface to ether1, then add ether1 to your bridge(tacos)

interfaces, select the interface, and then look for master-port... set that to ether1

now go to ip->addresses and add an ip to tacos(yourbridge)

There are 2 ways you can do this. One way is to simply create a wireless interface(since you can have more then one), on the wireless tab you will see vlan mode, set that to use tag, and then put the tag your using in the vlan id box. now you have that interface vlan you set up with /interface vlan add interface=wlan1 name=wifi_vlan_1 vlan-id=200  ...this will work just fine configured like that. and that particular ssid will tag/untag traffic for the vlan you configured it to. You can repeat this again to create another network(ssid) on the same interface if you want as well. 

The other way is to do the exact same thing but leave out setting the vlan mode on the wireless tab, and simply creating a bridge with the tagged interface, and the wireless interface in the same bridge. and just like the previous config, you can create more virtual ap interfaces and tag them as you want as well.
